text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘Migration is changing.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Migrants bring economic benefits to their host country.’
How could you test this claim?
You should consider the types of information, sources of evidence or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one opinion from Harry’s statement.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify one prediction from Erin’s statement.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why Erin’s statement may be biased.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Harry’s or Erin’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to encourage migrants to come and work in their country.
The following actions are being considered:
• giving financial support for businesses to employ migrants
• relaxing restrictions on migration
• offering language and cultural courses to migrants.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
